Step: #183
Sūtra involved: 6.1.102 प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः
Issue: Under 6.1.84 (एकः पूर्वपरयोः), an ekādeśa replaces both the preceding and following letters. The engine computes the correct surface string rAmAs. However, its internal parts array ([["rAm", "prakriti", "rAma"], ["As", "sup", "As"]]) reveals it stripped the ending from the prakṛti and glued the entire ekādeśa 'ā' onto the suffix piece.
Classification: Display/Engine structural artefact. This does not violate Pāṇinian logic textually, but it represents a slightly clunky programmatic way of handling a single substitute that straddles two morphological boundaries.
notes.author: me
notes.verdict: Claude 2026-11-16 — Surface rāmās is right; the parts array [rām|prakṛti][ās|sup] puts the ekādeśa on the suffix. That is a representation choice, not a śāstra error: Kāśikā 6.1.85 antādivacca says the ekādeśa counts as the end of the preceding AND the beginning of the following, so it belongs to both. Nothing to fix in the engine. Nice-to-have, not done: colour the ekādeśa letter as shared. Reopen only if a later rule reads the wrong side.

notes.text:
अक्-वर्णात् प्रथमा-द्वितीया-विभक्त्योः अजादि प्रत्यये परे पूर्वपरयोः एकः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः भवति ।
स्वौजसमौट्छष्टाभ्याम्भिस्ङेभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसिभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसोसाम्ङ्योस्सुप् ४.१.२ इति सूत्रेण प्रथमाविभक्तेः द्वितीयाविभक्तेः च प्रत्येकं त्रयः त्रयः प्रत्ययाः विधीयन्ते । एतेषु औट्, शस्, अम्, ओ, जस् - एते पञ्च प्रत्ययाः अजादयः सन्ति । एतेभ्यः पञ्चभ्यः प्रत्ययेभ्यः कश्चन प्रत्ययः अक्-वर्णान्त-शब्दात् विधीयते चेत् सुबन्तप्रक्रियायाम् अक्-वर्णस्य प्रत्ययादिवर्णेन सह पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घादेशः भवति ।
अस्य सूत्रस्य प्रयोगः केवलम् अक्-वर्णान्तशब्दानाम् प्रथमा-द्वितीया-विभक्त्योः प्रक्रियायाम् एव भवति । सोदाहरणम् परिगणनम् एतादृशम् —
१. अकारान्तशब्दाः —
अकारान्तशब्देभ्यः जस्/शस्-प्रत्यये परे प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः ६.१.१०२ इत्यनेन पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घैकादेशे कृते रूपं सिद्ध्यति । यथा —

बाल + जस् [प्रथमाबहुवचनस्य प्रत्ययः]
→ बाल + अस् [चुटू १.३.७ इत्यनेन जकारस्य इत्संज्ञा । तस्य लोपः १.३.९ इति लोपः]
→ बालास् [अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः ६.१.१०१ इत्यनेन सवर्णदीर्घे प्राप्ते, तं परत्वात् बाधित्वा प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः ६.१.१०२ इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः आकारः भवति ।]

1. Collapsing Ekādeśa and Substitution into One Sūtra (Engine Defect)
Step: #183
Sūtras involved: 6.1.102 प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः AND 6.1.103 तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि.
Issue: The engine jumps directly from rAmaas to rAmAn in a single step (#183) citing only 6.1.103. This is a severe violation of Pāṇinian mechanics and Engine Principle #3 (One sūtra = one operation).
First, 6.1.102 must apply to perform the pūrvasavarṇadīrgha (rāma + as → rāmās).
Only then can 6.1.103 apply. The very word tasmāt ("after that") in 6.1.103 explicitly requires the elongation from 6.1.102 to have already occurred to trigger the 's' → 'n' substitution (rāmās → rāmān).
Classification: Engine defect (Major). The engine has hardcoded 6.1.103 to perform both the vowel sandhi and the consonant substitution simultaneously. Rule 6.1.102 is missing entirely.

1. Collapsing Ekādeśa and Substitution into One Sūtra (Engine Defect)
Step: #183
Sūtras involved: 6.1.102 प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः AND 6.1.103 तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि.
Issue: The engine jumps directly from rAmaas to rAmAn in a single step (#183) citing only 6.1.103. This is a severe violation of Pāṇinian mechanics and Engine Principle #3 (One sūtra = one operation).
First, 6.1.102 must apply to perform the pūrvasavarṇadīrgha (rāma + as → rāmās).
Only then can 6.1.103 apply. The very word tasmāt ("after that") in 6.1.103 explicitly requires the elongation from 6.1.102 to have already occurred to trigger the 's' → 'n' substitution (rāmās → rāmān).
Classification: Engine defect (Major). The engine has hardcoded 6.1.103 to perform both the vowel sandhi and the consonant substitution simultaneously. Rule 6.1.102 is missing entirely.

Classification: Display/Engine structural artefact.

notes.verdict: Claude 2026-11-16 — On merit: right that the parts array shows one side taking the whole ekādeśa (rāma+au → stem rAmO, sup ''; rāma+as → stem rAm, sup As), while Kāśikā 6.1.85 antādivat/ādivat makes it both the end of the stem and the start of the suffix. The surface form is right and the only rules that read the split (pada/bha/sup-ness of the result) see the merged tape. It is a display and token problem, not a wrong form: S184 (ekādeśa as one shared token); no new work.
